neighbours.label: instrumental music-making of any kind: musical instruments and the people who play, compose for or build them (orchestras, violinists, guitarists, pianists, game and film composers); singing, rap, acting, dance, writing and visual art in the same frames stay low
fire: Late at night, my neighbour practises scales on the trumpet.
The quartet's second violinist tuned her instrument before the concert.
A self-taught guitarist recorded the whole album in his bedroom.
For the film, the composer wrote a theme for solo piano.
After lunch, the school orchestra rehearsed Beethoven in the gym.
On the subway platform, a saxophonist played for tips.
My grandfather built banjos in his workshop and played them at fairs.
The game's soundtrack was recorded with live strings and a harp.
quiet: Late at night, my neighbour practises lines for her play.
The choir's second soprano warmed up her voice before the service.
A self-taught rapper recorded the whole mixtape in his bedroom.
For the magazine, the novelist wrote a story about her childhood.
After lunch, the school debate team rehearsed arguments in the gym.
On the subway platform, a breakdancer performed for tips.
My grandfather built chairs in his workshop and sold them at fairs.
The game's artwork was painted by hand in watercolour.

notes: Coverage follow-up (new label, reason written in concept-maps/COVERAGE.md before this test): the held classical-music label (coverage #1046) covered 1/16; the misses were music-making of every kind. Exploration probes (two rounds, 24 sentences, none reused here) found instruments, players and composers strong in any genre, while singing, choirs, rap, DJs and the record business stayed low, so the label claims instrumental music-making and puts vocal music among the near misses.
